questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the city had a lot to offer, to get out of my comfort zone, improving my German

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The city, the uni, the people - everything there was amazing. But the bureaucracy, in particular all the papers that you need to sign and promise this and that - it felt like I was always under suspicion, and that I had to be able to predict the future and stick to a hypothetical plan all the time. I always felt uncomfortable getting a mail from the exchange offices or logging in here.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: FU did a good job providing the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange office (International and Erasmus) were, once again, sharp to address the most practical and relevant stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I got a response within 48 hours, sometimes on the same day!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Facebook groups for Danish expats - I benefit from the community there, but it is difficult and scammers are everywhere.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Check the rental prices for rooms in the area before signing a contract.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get some papers in a mail, you sign them and send back. If any questions, they are quick to answer.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: mail

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was one class where basic information was not clearly communicated since the professor did not use any of the course/learning portals. So I had to skip the course last minute, because I realized quite late that I was already behind.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask them, they are really nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The professors I had were very involving and had a great interest in hearing our inputs.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more activating, the structure with 3 ECTS for participation and 7 for term paper seem to work okay - students are motivated to read syllabus and participate. The exams are free written term papers, and the professors were good at making sure we could pitch ideas, give feedback, present results and make sure we did not get stuck. So I felt like I was also getting more directly involved in the academic practice, and could take ownership of my learning.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Genderperspectives in peace- and conflict studies
Politics of Trade
Automatic text analysis in R
International organizations in times of crisis
Environmental Governance in fast-growing economies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend courses by Lora Anne Viola, Bettina Engels and Sünje Paasch-Colberg.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was good, public transportation was free when you had the student card, so I won't complain here.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Clubs were more expensive. Everything else was a bliss.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports activities were good, the international office was good at making trips, but we could have used a tour to see the more informal social life at uni - like the student cafés or where to look for parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore the historical sites, go to the clubs, look at the museums, see some concerts and talk to some people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Same as above

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language and easy-going-ness of the international office

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take some courses with group work - give yourself time to explore the city - take a language course to get to know other exchange students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not important to go to the Bürgeramt. It has genuinely been a waste of time and resources for my part.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Again: The bureaucracy

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
